and 2 NEAR as `2.00`. All 3 visible tests pass. I didn't run the hidden tests, since I can't see them, so I haven't checked the round-trip requirement beyond the visible cases.

If an amount has non-zero digits past the second decimal, they are kept rather than rounded. Rounding would break the requirement that `parseNear(formatNear(x))` equals `x`. So a value like 1.123 NEAR shows as `1.123`, which is more than two places but loses nothing. If the hidden tests expect exactly two places even for those values, they would fail. I judged the round-trip rule to be the stricter requirement.
